# Pack-boundary denylist
#
# One sha256 per line. Each digest is the hash of a NORMALIZED term:
# lowercased, every run of non-alphanumeric characters collapsed to a single
# space, trimmed. Multi-word names are stored as their normalized n-gram
# string. `scripts/check_pack_boundary.py` checks every 1-, 2- and 3-gram of
# repo content against this list; CI fails on a hit.
#
# Never write a term in plaintext here, in a comment, in a commit message or
# in a PR. The names were deliberately redacted from repo text; a plaintext
# list would publish exactly what the redaction removed. The scan itself only
# ever reports file:line plus the matching digest.
#
# To add a term:
#     python scripts/check_pack_boundary.py --hash "the term"
# then append the printed digest below (sorted order is a convention, not a
# requirement) and rerun the scan.
#
# Watch the word count. The scanner checks 1-, 2- and 3-grams, so a term whose
# normalized form runs longer than three words can never match and becomes
# silent dead weight: once it is a digest, nothing here can tell it apart from
# a working entry. `--hash` warns when you hand it one. For a longer name, pick
# the most distinctive three-word span of it instead.
#
# Known tradeoff: sha256 of a well-known name is recoverable by anyone who
# guesses the name. This is not secrecy against determined analysis. It keeps
# the names out of repo text, out of diffs and out of CI logs.
#
# STATUS: DRAFT seed, assembled from general knowledge of widely known branded
# practice, healing and self-development frameworks. Tyler holds the
# authoritative off-repo list from the deliverability audit's provenance pass
# and should extend or replace this seed.
